newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Clinton misunderstands situation, HK's Tung says.
newsitem.headline: Clinton misunderstands situation, HK's Tung says.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's remarks about the future of civil liberties in Hong Kong show people overseas have been misled about the situation, the territory's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, said on Thursday.

Clinton told a White House news conference on Tuesday that Hong Kong might be of much less value to China if the civil liberties of its people were crushed after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule in July.

"I'm not so sure that it can exist with all of its potential to help China modernise its own economy and open opportunities for its own people, if the civil liberties of the people are crushed," Clinton said.

Asked for a response to Clinton's comments, Tung told Hong Kong reporters in Beijing: "I think there are certain sectors of people around the world who are concerned. But I think they are being misled."
"I think they should spend more time to really understand what is really going on in Hong Kong."
Tung said polls conducted by foreign chambers of commerce in Hong Kong showed a high level of business confidence in Hong Kong's future after the handover to China.

Tung travelled to Beijing for a two-day meeting of the Preparatory Committee, the China-appointed caucus responsible for shaping Hong Kong's future when China resumes sovereignty after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
High on the agenda of the meeting, which starts on Friday, will be a proposal to repeal several of Hong Kong's laws on civil liberties, including part of the Bill of Rights.
The plan sparked outrage in Hong Kong. Britain has lodged a strong protest against the proposal.
